message.content:
Littelfuse polymer ESD suppressors (PulseGuard, AXGD1, PGB1, XGD) are voltage-dependent polymer devices. Classification is under heading 8533 (resistors) or 8536 (apparatus for protecting electrical circuits, for a voltage not exceeding 1,000 V) or 8541 (varistors).

Heading 8533 includes varistors, which are voltage-dependent resistors. Subheading 8533.40 covers other variable resistors, including rheostats and potentiometers, and varistors fall there. Polymer ESD suppressors are non-linear voltage-dependent resistive devices, so they would be varistors under 8533.40.

Several CBP rulings on Littelfuse PulseGuard ESD suppressors classified them under 8533.40.8000 or 8536.30.8000. I recall that NY N-rulings put the polymer ESD suppressors in 8536.30.8030, "Other apparatus for protecting electrical circuits, for a voltage not exceeding 1,000 V." Surface-mount ones were often placed in 8533.40.80. The statistical suffix for 8536.30.80 is 8000 (post-2022, with 8536.30.8000 as the line).

I considered the Explanatory Notes: 8536.30 covers fuses, circuit breakers, surge suppressors, and similar devices. The polymer ESD devices operate by switching, as a voltage-variable material, in a way similar to a surge suppressor. I will go with 8536.30.8000.
